from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of a squirrel gathering nuts.",
            "Its velocity is the rate of position change.",
            "We call this rate the derivative.",
            "Accumulated distance is the integral of velocity.",
            "They are two sides of one coin."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Bridge: The Velocity-Position Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        squirrel_dot = Dot(color="#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(squirrel_dot, "B2")
        self.play(Create(squirrel_dot))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(path_line, "B3")
        self.play(Create(path_line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(velocity_arrow, "B3")
        self.play(GrowArrow(velocity_arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[3]))
        # Visualize area as a rectangle under the velocity arrow
        area = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.5, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#FFFF33", stroke_width=0)
        self.place_at_grid(area, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF33")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[4]))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.",
            "Differentiation finds the slope at a point.",
            "Integration sums up tiny pieces to reconstruct.",
            "They effectively undo each other.",
            "A powerful mathematical harmony emerges here."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Inverse Operation", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**2 + 1, x_range=[0, 4], color="#ADD8E6")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFA500")
        dot = Dot(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5), color=RED)
        # Fix: axes.get_derivative_slope is not a method on Axes. Use the derivative of the function directly.
        slope = 0.5 * 0.5  # Derivative of 0.25*x^2 is 0.5*x, at x=0.5 -> 0.25. Scaled by axes.
        tangent = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=RED).rotate(np.arctan(0.25)).move_to(dot)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(tangent))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.5, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(rects))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Demonstrate getting thinner
        new_rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.1, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(rects, new_rects))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeOut(dot), FadeOut(tangent), FadeOut(new_rects))
        self.play(Create(curve.copy().set_color("#00FF00")))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Integrating a rate gives net change.", "Area under the curve measures total accumulation.", "This is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus."]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 - 0.5 * x + 1, x_range=[0, 4])
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show f(x) and its integral function F(x)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        f_label = MathTex("f(x)").next_to(curve, UP)
        self.add(axes, curve, f_label)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight small increment dx on the x-axis #FF00FF.
        # Show the small area increment dF = f(x)dx #00FFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        dx_rect = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=1, color="#00FFFF").set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        dx_rect.move_to(axes.c2p(2, 0.5))
        self.add(dx_rect)
        
        dF_label = MathTex("dF = f(x)dx", color="#00FFFF").next_to(dx_rect, UP)
        self.add(dF_label)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Connect derivative of F(x) to f(x) #FFFF00.
        # Display fundamental theorem formula clearly #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        ftc_formula = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(ftc_formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

        # Define visual elements
        slope_icon = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=BLUE).add_tip()
        area_icon = Rectangle(height=1.0, width=1.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept using a squirrel gathering nuts. If we know how fast the squirrel moves at any moment (velocity), we can figure out its total distance (integral). Conversely, if we know its total distance over time, we can find its speed at any specific point (derivative).
sections.example: A squirrel runs along a branch. The rate of change of its position is its velocity (Derivative); the accumulated area under its velocity-time graph is the distance covered (Integral).

sections.title: Visualizing the Inverse Operation
sections.content: Explain that differentiation and integration are inverse processes, similar to 'undoing' an action. Use a graphical animation showing the slope of a tangent line (differentiation) being 're-built' by summing up infinitely thin rectangles (integration).
sections.example: Visualize a curve f(x). Differentiation finds the steepness (slope) at one point; Integration 'collects' these steepness values to reconstruct the original shape of the curve.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
sections.content: Formally connect the two: If you integrate a rate of change function from a to b, you get the net change in the original function. Emphasize that the 'Area Under the Curve' is not just a shape, but a measure of accumulation.
sections.example: If f'(x) is the rate at which water fills a tank, the integral of f'(x) from time 0 to 5 gives the total volume of water added to the tank in those 5 minutes.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = Slope/Rate of Change; Integral = Area/Accumulation. The Fundamental Theorem links these two concepts, allowing us to compute complex areas simply by evaluating the function at its endpoints.
sections.example: A 'Robot Arm' movement path: The sensor measures velocity (derivative). By integrating that data, the controller calculates the exact position of the arm relative to the start.
